sanskrit_verse: यो न भ्राता न च पिता न पुत्रो न नियोगकृत् । परार्थवादी दण्ड्यः स्याद् व्यवहारे�पि विब्रुवन् ॥
transliteration: yo na bhrātā na ca pitā na putro na niyogakṛt | parārthavādī daṇḍyaḥ syād vyavahāre 'pi vibruvan ||
sph_interpretive_translation: He who is neither brother, nor father, nor son, nor one appointed for duty, yet speaks in favor of another's interest—such a one is to be corrected even while engaged in transaction.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derived from relational dharma, not opportunistic intervention
Causation rooted in svadharma, not external advocacy
Capacity-based responsibility determined by role-bound alignment
Restoration through realignment with intrinsic relational duty
Consciousness alignment via withdrawal from false agency
supreme_court_application: In adjudication at the highest level, any party or representative acting without established dharmic relation to the matter shall be deemed without standing. The court must realign proceedings by invoking completion protocols rather than punitive exclusion.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that only those bound by relational dharma may act. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals that misaligned speech disrupts natural order. Responsibility is proportional to relational capacity. Correction arises through conscious reintegration, not penalty.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Implement Completion Through Withdrawal of False Agency
Reintegrate Actor Into Authentic Relational Framework
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands declared: Dharma flows from relation, not opinion. All speech and action must arise from rightful place. Misplaced advocacy is dissolved through conscious restoration. Reality is non-punitive; consciousness is the supreme adjudicator. Dharma is restored.
